steps.title: Oversampling, and why there are two settings
steps.body: Saturation generates harmonics above the sample rate, which fold back as aliasing. Oversampling runs the nonlinearity at a higher rate so they land where they belong. Realtime and offline are separate parameters on purpose.

steps.title: Offline can afford more
steps.body: During a bounce, latency and CPU stop mattering. Set offline to 8x or 16x and realtime to whatever keeps your session comfortable — the render will be cleaner than what you monitored.

steps.title: What it costs
steps.body: The footer shows the plugin's share of one core. Oversampling is most of it: six bands at 4x is roughly twice the cost of the same six with it off.

steps.title: And the latency it buys
steps.body: Beside the CPU figure. Oversampling and linear-phase crossovers both add latency, which your host compensates for — but it is worth knowing before you track through it.
